machatzit-hashekel/4:ב: And furthermore, Tosafot in Avodah Zarah are stringent, etc. — meaning in chametz; and see Shach in Yoreh De'ah siman 108, note 13. With this the proof of Maharil is refuted — Maharil in siman 186: "It seems you were in doubt, since chametz is in any amount, whether reicha is a matter," etc. — and it appears there is no distinction for one who holds reicha is not a matter; and he brought proof from Levi, who permits meat of a slaughtered animal roasted with nevelah meat in every case, even when both are the same species, even for one who holds same species in same species in any amount; and so is proven there in chapter 26, where they challenge one who holds [the prohibition is] on account of mixture of flavors: what difference to me kid and kid, what difference to me kid and lamb — let us say according to one who holds kid and kid, which is same species in same species, and according to R' Yehuda and R' Yehoshua ben Levi, same species in same species in any amount, but even kid and lamb, which is species in a different species. And Rav also holds same species in same species in any amount — end of Maharil's words. His intention is what they said in chapter 26, daf 76: it was stated — meat of a slaughtered animal that was roasted with nevelah meat, lean: Rav said forbidden — what is the reason? reicha is a matter; and Levi said permitted — reicha is not a matter. They challenged him: "One does not roast two Paschal [lambs] together" because of mixture — what, is it not mixture of flavors? And this is difficult for Levi — not on account of mixture of bodies (and the reason for mixture of bodies or their flavor is that thereby the Pesach is eaten not according to its requirement). The answer is from what the conclusion teaches: even kid and lamb. If not on account of bodies, why does it teach even kid and lamb? If not on account of mixture of flavors, what difference to me kid and lamb, what difference to me kid and kid? Rather, what — mixture of flavors, and it is permitted; let it be a refutation of Rav — end of the Gemara. And Maharil infers from the challengers' question that challenges Rav: why "even kid and lamb" — what is the extra matter in kid and lamb more than kid and kid? If not on account of mixture of flavors. And if not, even for us who hold klaiv (taste is nullified), nevertheless in chametz reicha is a matter, for Levi concedes that there is still a minute amount. Rather, Rav holds that reicha is a full flavor; if so, kid and lamb is properly an extra matter — according to one who holds kid and kid, which is same species in same species, and the baraita follows R' Yehuda, who holds same species in same species in any amount, and if so it is forbidden even if reicha is not a matter, for there is still a minute amount; rather, even kid and lamb, which is species in a different species, is forbidden because it is a full flavor. Rather, perforce one must say that the Gemara holds that if reicha is a matter it is a full flavor, and if it is not a matter, even a minute amount of flavor does not exist; and if so, it properly challenges: what difference to me kid, etc. And so wrote Magen Avraham — according to the Rif his proof is refuted, for at first glance one could say against Maharil's proof that even if we say Levi concedes that there is still a minute amount, nevertheless it challenges properly: what difference to me kid, etc., even though kid and kid is same species in same species; nevertheless, the baraita deals with l'chatchila, for it teaches "one does not roast," and regarding l'chatchila there is no distinction between same species and different species, for whatever forbids in same species b'dieved on account of forbidding in any amount in a different species, in any case l'chatchila is forbidden, for we hold one does not nullify a prohibition l'chatchila; and one must say this is difficult for Maharil — behold Tosafot there explain Rashi that Levi disagrees only b'dieved but l'chatchila concedes it is forbidden; if so, what does the Gemara challenge Levi from the baraita "one does not roast two Paschal [lambs]" — behold the baraita deals with l'chatchila; perforce Levi permits even l'chatchila, and this is difficult for Maharil according to the questioner's view that Levi concedes there is still a minute amount. And therefore in chametz reicha is a matter — if so, it itself is difficult: why does Levi permit l'chatchila? Behold one does not nullify a prohibition l'chatchila. And if so, it does not challenge Levi at all from the baraita "one does not roast two Paschal [lambs]"; perforce one must say the Gemara holds this is not called nullifying a prohibition, since he does not intend to nullify — as below siman 453, seif 3; and see Taz and Yoreh De'ah siman 84, note 45, in Shach, and in many places. And therefore Maharil's proof does not stand, for perforce there is certainly a minute amount; kid and lamb is properly an extra matter, for it is a different species, and we would have thought reicha is only a minute amount, and even l'chatchila in a different species is permitted because he does not intend to nullify — it teaches us that it is a full flavor; and this is said to reject the questioner's view to Maharil, who would hold Rav holds a full flavor and Levi, whom we hold like, at least holds a minute amount of flavor. But according to the Rif, for Rav himself there is only a minute amount of flavor; if so, certainly for Levi there is not even a minute amount — for if not, what is Levi's reason? It should not depend on whether Levi holds same species in same species is nullified; if so, their dispute does not depend at all on the law of whether reicha is a matter, but rather on same species in same species in any amount or not; and one would have to say they dispute in general regarding same species in same species — perforce Levi holds that even for one who holds same species in same species in any amount, nevertheless reicha is not a matter, for in any case there is no minute amount of flavor; rather, the Rif holds we rule like Rav against Levi, for the reasons the Rif wrote there, but one cannot rule like Rav since Rav concedes it is only a minute amount of flavor. Rather, Rav according to his reasoning of same species in same species in any amount, and meat of a slaughtered animal with nevelah is same species in same species. And if so, for us who hold same species in same species is nullified, one cannot rule like Rav; if so, in chametz, for we hold it forbids in any amount, we hold like Rav that reicha is a matter. And therefore Maharil's proof is refuted — perforce it must be so according to the Rif: that which the Gemara challenges Rav, why "even kid and lamb" more — it should have said: if not on account of mixture of flavors; if so, why is kid and lamb, which is species in a different species, forbidden, since even for Rav reicha is only a minute amount? Perforce one must say that nevertheless, since the baraita deals with l'chatchila, for it teaches "one does not roast," etc., and regarding l'chatchila for Rav even a different species is forbidden, for one does not nullify a prohibition l'chatchila; perforce one must say this is called intending to nullify. And nevertheless for Levi it challenges properly, for perforce for Levi even l'chatchila is permitted, for perforce for Levi even a minute amount of flavor does not exist, as above. And therefore Maharil's proof is correct, for it challenges properly: what difference to me kid, etc.; for although this is same species in same species and that is a different species, nevertheless, since the baraita deals with l'chatchila, and regarding l'chatchila there is no distinction between same species and different species, for one does not nullify a prohibition l'chatchila, as above:
